title: Module quiz: Working with an AI, responsibly

questions.stem: A team uses Claude to draft a monthly variance narrative from a finance export. After a few clean months the lead proposes two changes: Claude will also decide which variances reach the directors, and the figure-by-figure review stops. Which response applies both pages?

options.text: Keep the judgment call with a person and keep verifying every number against its source
options.says: Judgment that carries accountability stays with a person, and figures are checked against the source of record however clean past drafts were (page 1 delegation table; page 2 checking routine).

options.text: Let Claude take the judgment call, since clean drafts show sound judgment, and keep verifying numbers
options.says: Ruled out because the table gives "Decide which variances matter to the board" to a person, as judgment with accountability, and a clean run does not move it.

options.text: Drop the verification, since clean drafts show the numbers are right, and keep the judgment call human
options.says: Ruled out because "A good draft does not show the figures were right", so a run of clean drafts is no reason to stop verifying.

options.text: Let Claude take both, and ask it to flag any figure it doubts
options.says: Ruled out because "Self-reported confidence is not a measure of accuracy", and a flag from the model replaces neither the person nor the check.

origin.section: Delegate: which steps go to Claude

questions.stem: A support lead gets a drafted reply to an angry customer that is accurate but reads like a legal notice. The lead needs the next attempt to come out right. Which change to the request follows the pages?

options.text: Open with a role line: "You are a world-class customer-care writer"
options.says: Ruled out because a role line names no reader or purpose, and the page says to "Add what a colleague new to the job would need".

options.text: Send the identical request again and keep the first answer that sounds friendly
options.says: Ruled out because "Regenerating the same request and hoping is the reflex", and an identical request is a second guess.

options.text: Describe the audience, add one sample in the voice wanted, then compare
options.says: The description should say who reads it and show the target style, and the iterate-not-re-roll method compares the new result with the last (page 1, describe; page 2, iterate).

options.text: Move to a higher tier, which follows loose instructions better
options.says: Ruled out because "the description is where most of the quality is decided", and a higher tier does not know the readers either.

origin.section: Describe: the three things to say

questions.stem: A consultant forwards a client a report that Claude drafted. The client later finds a wrong number in it. Who answers for the mistake, and what should have happened first?

options.text: The tool's provider answers, since its software produced the number
options.says: Ruled out because "You own what you send, whoever drafted it".

options.text: The sender owns the work and should have verified the figures at their source
options.says: The sender owns what was sent, and figures are checked against the source of record before release (page 2, take responsibility and the checking routine; page 1, where checking every figure sits with a person or a script).

options.text: The recipient answers, since the number was accepted without question
options.says: Ruled out because "the person who relied on it will not distinguish between you and the tool", so blame does not move to the reader.

options.text: The sender answers, but only if the work lacked a note about the AI's part
options.says: Ruled out because "An error in AI-assisted work is your error to correct", with or without a disclosure note; disclosure is a separate duty.

questions.stem: A team asks Claude to fill a supplier price table from a PDF. Every row comes back filled, including one cost the PDF never states, and the table goes to the finance director today. Which pair of actions fits both pages?

options.text: Send the table on as filled, trusting the figures that fit the layout
options.says: Ruled out because "Readers check tone and grammar, which are visible, and skip figures and citations", which is where the damage is.

options.text: Ask for a confidence beside each entry, then keep the entries marked high
options.says: Ruled out because "Self-reported confidence is not a measure of accuracy".

options.text: Fill the unknown cost with the average of the other rows and label it an estimate
options.says: Ruled out because "the careless move is to fill the gap with an estimate", and a label on an invented value still puts it in the table.

options.text: Have it flag missing values, keep the gap, and check the rest at source
options.says: Page 1 puts the rule in the description ("say so rather than estimating"), page 2 says a declared gap is information to keep, and the figures that remain are checked against the source of record.
